body: Missing double-checked locking: after acquiring the write lock the cache isn't re-checked. On a cold start (or after a failed load) N concurrent requests all see `ret == nil`, then queue on `Lock()` and each one re-reads/re-parses assets-manifest.json (or re-fetches from the CDN) serially while holding the global exclusive lock. Re-check `entryPointAssetsCache` (when `cfg.Env != setting.Dev`) right after `Lock()` and return early if another goroutine already populated it — or use `sync.Once`/singleflight.

I/O now runs while the global write lock is held, and it uses the request's `ctx`. If the CDN path is enabled, a slow HTTP fetch blocks every caller of GetWebAssets (index page, /api/frontend/assets, and the panic-recovery page in middleware/recovery.go). Also, if the first request's context is canceled, the fetch fails and every waiter repeats it. Do the load outside the lock (or with a detached context via singleflight) and only take the write lock to publish the result.

On error, `result` is nil and this overwrites whatever was cached before with nil, so one transient failure throws away the last good value. In Dev mode that means a failed read clears the cache for everyone else. Only store the result when `err == nil`.

In Dev mode every call now takes the exclusive lock and re-reads the manifest file, so all index/asset requests are serialized behind file I/O. That's probably acceptable for dev, but the read/parse could happen without the lock, with the lock held only to swap the pointer.
